title: Prose written once, code changed since
problem: From v10.0.0 to v11.3.0 the items whose prose names a file changed after the line grew from 31 to 82, and no release lowered the count. Eight claims the prose makes about the code are refuted by it at v11.3.0, and four of them are older than the code that refutes them. ESI.ts's own gates pass at every release: nothing it runs compares a sentence with the file it names.
background: These judgments were written by Claude, an agent, at the owner's request (the stage 28 plan of Ingesting a codebase, docs/spec/11-ingesting-a-codebase.md, where the owner asked that CSH be shown as a static analysis tool whose outcome is convergence, gaps and indeterminate). They are candidates: nothing is approved, and the owner may revise any of them.

ESI.ts is evaluated from outside, read-only, at each release tag (csh history prose-drift --from v10.0.0 --to v11.3.0). Each stage is the profile in subjects/esi-ts/csh run at that tag. The stage records stay out of git, since their reports quote ESI.ts, which is GPL-3.0; this sheet holds only identifiers, paths, spans, commits and counts, and continuous integration rebuilds the stages and compares the sheet.

How each practice is judged on its own terms: the charter and guides by review, the scenarios and tests by passing, the security model by its own audit script. All pass at every release. Stale prose is a heuristic: a line is stale when a file it names changed after the line was last written, which says the line should be re-read, not that it is wrong. Fact-conflicts and claim-conflicts are not heuristics: the code or another document refutes the sentence.

goal: Every line that names a file is re-read when the file changes, and every fact the prose states about the code is either a claim CSH checks or generated from the code. The count of stale-prose items falls at each release instead of rising, and no claim the code refutes survives a release.

rca.q: Why does stale prose only grow from release to release?
rca.a: Lines are written once, when a feature lands, and the files they name go on changing. Review reads the lines a change edits, not the lines that name the files it changes, so nothing brings an old line back for reading. The two jumps are the releases that added documents: v10.0.0 (the charter) and v11.0.0 (the guides from 15 to 27).

rca.q: Why do refuted claims survive releases that pass every gate?
rca.a: The facts they state (the Node floor, the entry points, the unit tier's size, the compatibility date) are hand-typed in prose. ESI.ts generates some counts into prose through markers (etc/doc-metrics.json), but these sentences are outside the markers, so no generator or check touches them. Four of the eight are older than the code that refutes them: the code moved and the sentence did not.
rca.depth: Two whys: hand-typed, and outside the markers.

rca.q: Why are eight requirements unverified though every gate passes?
rca.a: Their Verified-by lines name prose (code review, a process) rather than a check, and no test cites them. The status column says Enforced or Practised regardless. Nothing ties a status to a mechanism the repository holds.
rca.depth: One why: the status is asserted, not derived.

whys.a: A file it names changed after the line was last written.

whys.q: Why was the line not updated with the file?
whys.a: The change that edited the file did not touch the document, and review looked only at the change.

whys.q: Why did review not look at the document?
whys.a: Nothing links a file to the lines that name it: the link exists only as a path inside a sentence.
The guides and the charter are checked for their own form (Markdown lint, EARS audit, link checks), never against the history of what they name.

whys.q: Why are they checked only for form?
whys.a: Each practice is judged on its own terms, and no practice owns the relation between a sentence and a file.
whys.root: No practice owns the relation between prose and the code it names.

countermeasures.what: Re-read, at each release, the lines csh overview lists as stale-prose for that release, and update or date each one. Lines that are history rather than claims (a changelog, an amendment log) are marked as such so they stop counting.

Write each hand-typed fact about the code (Node floor, entry points, tier sizes, CI jobs, compatibility date) through the doc-metrics markers, or as a claim in the profile's ProseAboutCode, so the code is its one source.
Derive a requirement's status from what verifies it: Enforced only when a mechanism the repository holds, or a test that cites the requirement, is named. ESI.ts issues #634 and #639 track this.

plan.what: Open ESI.ts issues for the refuted claims and the unverified requirements (#631 to #634, #639, #640)
Decide C1 to C3 and apply them in ESI.ts
Re-run csh history prose-drift after the next release and compare

terms.meaning: a line that names a file changed after the line was last written: a suggestion to re-read it, not a proof it is wrong
